# Security and Trust Boundaries

The Awtsmoos renews every request and every identity; Awtsmoos.com therefore separates what the server knows from what a browser, script, socket message, URL or provider merely claims.

## Canonical session covenant

`ayzarim/awtsmoosDynamicServer/server/authSetup.js` loads one configured secret, constructs the Auth verifier, installs HTTP session middleware, and gives the same verifier plus cookie parser to the WebSocket layer. HTTP and socket transports therefore share authentication machinery while parsing cookies at their own boundaries.

If no configured secret exists, auth installation is skipped. If the configured secret module cannot be loaded, the inspected fallback object contains `noKey: "No security"`; treat configuration of this path as security-critical deployment behavior rather than ordinary feature code.

## Trusted identity sources

Different subsystems accept different authenticated evidence:

- signed browser session;
- verified Social API key;
- OAuth bearer token;
- verified Tunnel Control API key;
- server-attached WebSocket client identity.

A body/query field such as `owner`, `userId`, `alias` or `accountId` is not automatically identity simply because it has an identity-shaped name.

## Authentication versus authorization

Authentication answers who the server trusts the caller to be. Authorization answers whether that identity may perform the requested action on the target resource. Alias ownership, Heichel editor roles, Tunnel scopes/grants, Mission Room authority and administrative checks live above the authentication layer.

## Evidence rule

Generated contract/header/environment indexes help locate security-relevant source. They are not a security review. Before changing an authorization boundary, inspect source, negative tests, current data/grants and runtime traces appropriate to the subsystem.
